sections.overall: A quiet-ish week in the rankings, despite there being one extra hour more than a typical week. The two standout matches were Kris Statlander vs Hikaru Shida (7.71) and Konosuke Takeshita (7.98) vs Daniel Garcia, both of which were main events on Wednesday and Saturday respectively. Plenty of team matches featured this week, with all each of the Tag and Trios divisions represented.
sections.mens: Takeshita's strong run continues, his International Title defence nearly enough to see him topple Darby. His already-high rating (the 'current factor') plus the Collision show and match having a small-ish number of votes, meant this was more of a consolidation of his rating. Mark Davis vs Jack Perry was another highlight (7.39), another strong addition to the Owen Hart Tournament.
sections.womens: Two great matches this week! As well as Wednesday's main event, we saw the strongest women's match in the Owen Hart Tournament so far, with the debuting Hazuki and Maya World (7). Shida does not quite crack the top 5 but hopefully her Lights Out Philly Street Fight is not the end of her opportunities.
sections.menstag: A plethora of teams to choose from in the Men's Tag division. The Death Riders duo of Moxley & PAC featured in two matches (one standard tag and within one Trio). Though they are a long way off the top-rated teams.
sections.womenstag: Welcome TayJay to the Women's Tag rankings! Although the 5 minute Eliminator challenge was far from a classic, it was refreshing to see Divine Dominion featured for more than a squash match, at least. Hopefully with more time the two teams will deliver more in their upcoming title match.
sections.trios: Two Trios matches this week, though neither received a great rating. The Conglomeration's Cassidy, O'Reilly & Strong's matches have not been setting the world alight - reflected in the Trios Title lanhuising low down in the Championship Rankings (see the new Championships section on the menu!)
